evidence: src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts private item(): `return new Item(d.sku, d.description, d.unitWeightGrams, d.reorderLevel);` builds an entity from a raw ItemTable record (persistence mapping)
src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts private bin(): `return new Bin(d.code, d.sku, d.quantity, d.maxWeightGrams);` builds an entity from a raw BinTable record (persistence mapping)

src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts pick(): `for (const data of await this.bins.holding(sku)) { const bin = new Bin(data.code, data.sku, data.quantity, data.maxWeightGrams);` turns table rows into entities inside the domain loop
src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts receive() and pick(): `await this.bins.store({ ...bin });` turns an entity back into a table record (persistence serialization)
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of what ReceivingService does is domain work. It checks that a received quantity is a positive whole number, spreads a pick across several bins, and asks the Item whether stock needs reordering. That all fits the business (domain) layer.

The file also does data-mapper work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer. The private item() and bin() methods, and the loop in pick(), turn raw table records (d.sku, d.unitWeightGrams, data.maxWeightGrams and so on) into domain objects, field by field. receive() and pick() also turn entities back into rows with `this.bins.store({ ...bin })`. So the service has to know the column layout of ItemTable and BinTable and how entities are stored. That is persistence logic and should sit in a repository or mapper in the persistence layer, with the domain getting whole Item and Bin objects.

Which modules the file imports is out of scope here and was not judged. Confidence is moderate because some designs accept this kind of mapping in an application service.

violations.message: The private item() and bin() methods and the loop in pick() build Item and Bin entities field by field from raw ItemTable/BinTable records. That row-to-entity mapping is persistence (infrastructure) work and belongs in a repository or mapper, not a domain service.
receive() and pick() turn Bin entities back into table records with `this.bins.store({ ...bin })`. Deciding how entities are stored is persistence (infrastructure) logic placed in the business layer.
